subject: general
question: The pH of gastric juice is _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pH of gastric juice is typically around **1.2**, indicating its highly acidic nature.
 
• This acidity is primarily due to the presence of **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** in the stomach.
 
• The acidic environment helps in the breakdown of food and activation of digestive enzymes such as **pepsin**.
 
• Hydrochloric acid in gastric juice also plays a crucial role in **killing harmful bacteria** and pathogens ingested with food.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**

 
 
• It is secreted by the parietal cells in the stomach lining.
 
• The concentration of hydrochloric acid in gastric juice is about 0.5% (5000 ppm).
 
 
 
• **Pepsin**
 
 
• Pepsin is a digestive enzyme that breaks down proteins into peptides.
 
• It is activated from its precursor, pepsinogen, in the presence of hydrochloric acid.
 
 
 
• **Gastric Mucosa**
 
 
• The inner lining of the stomach is called the gastric mucosa.
 
• It contains various glands that secrete mucus, hydrochloric acid, and digestive enzymes.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale**
 
 
• The pH scale measures the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.
 
• A pH value below 7 indicates acidity, 7 is neutral, and above 7 indicates alkalinity.
